criteria.criterion: CheckConfig in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs accepts an optional `skip_when_only` list. An absent list means the check always runs. Existing configurations parse unchanged.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, config.rs adds `#[serde(default)] pub skip_when_only: Option<Vec<String>>` to CheckConfig, with a doc comment. The test skip_when_only_is_optional_and_parsed_when_present parses REPO_CONFIG unchanged, asserts every check has None, then parses a copy with the key added. In checks.rs, skip_note returns None when the list is absent.

criteria.criterion: athena.toml is NOT modified. It must contain no `skip_when_only` key, so the gate's old parser accepts the landing commit. A note (docs or CHANGELOG) says enabling the key is a separate follow-up job after this one lands.
criteria.evidence: athena.toml is not in the diff stat, and `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- athena.toml` printed nothing. The repo-config test asserts no check carries the key. CHANGELOG.md says "This change does not set the key in athena.toml … enabling it is a separate follow-up job after this one lands", and M31 in enforcement.md says the same.

criteria.criterion: The check runner skips a check only when every changed path matches a named set in the configuration. An empty change list or any non-matching path runs the check. The skip is recorded in the run output with a note, not silently.
criteria.evidence: checks.rs skip_note returns None for an absent or empty pattern list or an empty change list, and returns Some only when `all` changed paths match some pattern. run.rs takes the paths from closing.candidate.changes and pushes skipped_run(spec, note), which records passed=true and note "not run: every changed path matches skip_when_only (...)". That note reaches the verifier brief's check detail. ChangeStatus has no Rename variant, so a rename cannot hide its source path.

criteria.criterion: The path-matching rules (including the `*.ext` suffix form matching at any depth) are documented in code comments or docs/enforcement.md.
criteria.evidence: The rules are documented in the path_matches doc comment in checks.rs, the CheckConfig field doc in config.rs and enforcement.md row M31. All three cover `dir/`, `*.ext` at any depth and exact paths.

criteria.criterion: docs/enforcement.md has a row for the new mechanism that names its tests.
criteria.evidence: Row M31 names a_studies_json_only_change_runs_every_check, a_check_without_a_skip_list_always_runs, an_empty_or_mixed_change_runs_the_check, a_docs_only_change_skips_and_says_so, path_patterns_match_by_directory_suffix_or_exact_path and skip_when_only_is_optional_and_parsed_when_present. The policy test every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`. All tests pass, including new unit tests for config parsing, path matching, and skip versus run decisions. Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both are clean.
criteria.evidence: `cargo test --locked`: every suite ok, 0 failed. The athena_core output includes the 5 new checks:: tests and the athena_data output includes config::tests::skip_when_only_is_optional_and_parsed_when_present, all ok. Clippy finished with no warnings and fmt --check printed nothing.

findings.summary: No test covers the skip wiring in the runner itself, only the helper functions.
findings.evidence: The tests cover skip_note, skipped_run and path_matches. Nothing exercises run.rs: no integration test confirms that a docs-only candidate's check is recorded as skipped while a code change still runs it. Removing the 4 added lines in run.rs would leave every test passing.

findings.summary: The files changed differ from the expected deliverables.
findings.evidence: The reading listed docs/decisions.md, run_pin_tests.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs, but none were modified. run.rs was modified but not listed. Nothing here breaks: all tests compile and pass. It may affect deliverable scoring, and the repository's decision log has no entry for this mechanism.

findings.summary: A skipped test-kind check is recorded as passed with tests_ran None, which bypasses the zero-tests rule.
findings.evidence: This is intended for prose-only changes. M31 could say outright that a skip overrides the kind=test rule that a test check which ran zero tests fails.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. It adds `skip_when_only`, an optional list of path patterns, to `CheckConfig` and passes it through to `CheckSpec` in both capabilities. The runner in run.rs now skips a check only when the change is not empty and every changed path matches a pattern. A skipped check is recorded as passed with a "not run: …" note. athena.toml is unchanged, which avoids the bootstrap failure that sank the last attempt, and CHANGELOG.md and enforcement.md row M31 both say that turning the key on is a separate follow-up job. Unit tests cover config parsing, path matching (including the `*.ext` form at any depth) and the skip-or-run decision. I ran `cargo test --locked` (all passed, including the 6 new tests and the test that checks enforcement.md's test names exist), clippy (clean), fmt (clean) and `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- athena.toml` (no output, so athena.toml is unchanged). There are two minor gaps and one nit: nothing tests the wiring in run.rs itself; some listed deliverables were not touched while run.rs, which was not listed, was; and skipping a test-kind check bypasses the zero-tests rule, which is intended but not stated in M31.
